mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which pressures firms to raise wages and prices, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below the market median at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly lower during triggered episodes compared to non-triggered periods at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% for three consecutive months signals an acceleration in economic activity and capacity utilization, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA +2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months indicates a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during co-decline episodes at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages by more than 1% in the same month signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-month MA +1% AND CPIAUCSL > 12-month MA +1% in the same month
regime_hint: dual inflation and rate tightening regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during such dual-trigger months at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% in a single month, combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE), indicates robust job creation without upward wage pressure, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA +2% AND UNRATE unchanged within ±0.1pp in the same month
regime_hint: strong job growth, stable wage environment
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during such episodes at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on negative relationship exists between real retail sales (RSAFS) and S&P 500 forward returns at a 5-day horizon: lower-than-expected monthly retail sales growth (vs. prior 12-month average) predicts negative short-term equity returns as consumer spending weakness quickly transmits to earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly RSAFS surprises and 5-day S&P 500 returns is not significantly negative at p<0.05 in out-of-sample tests.
